facts.fact: The ADEA peer review of September 2019 states under its norm on registration of learners that Zimbabwe has no learner tracking system and no individual learner identification system in place; copies of learners' birth certificates are kept at the schools.

systems.country_label: EMIS; Annual School Census (ASC), form ED 46
systems.platform: not stated; data captured to a central server at head office over a wide area network
systems.owner: Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education, Strategic Policy Planning, Research and Statistics Department, with the ICT department
systems.tiers: A 20-page annual questionnaire filled in by hand at about 8,953 schools and certified by the head; keyed at the district office and passed through the province to headquarters; in 2019 keyed centrally because of electricity and internet problems. Response rate 95% for 2019.

Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education
systems.tiers: Ministry; updated once a year; the census questionnaire is sent to the schools on it, known unregistered schools included

note: The system the report calls EMIS is the annual school census: the only entry it describes is the yearly ED 46 return, on paper at the school and keyed at the district. Its statements on budget line, donor top-up and the absence of an EMIS policy describe that census, so give no fact. The capture is an excerpt, cut off at the Norm 8 scoring tables. The report's higher and tertiary systems are outside the study's levels and are not listed.
